answer: An agent economy resists sybils by scoring each identity on an unbroken continuous-uptime streak. Random liveness beacons strike like a sudden gale, and only a node truly online answers every one in seconds. That streak is the anchor of its influence, which decays the instant a beacon is missed. An operator cramming many clones onto one machine chokes on CPU contention and drops beacons, so the whole flock slides back from the summit while a genuine lone node keeps its climb intact.
